problem: Autonomous exploration and spatial memory construction are usually decoupled: the agent explores with geometric occupancy grids or frontiers, then builds a scene graph offline. Geometry-centric exploration misses navigationally critical but geometrically ambiguous landmarks (doorways, stairs), and the semantic scene graph cannot guide exploration.
motivation: A structured global memory is needed for long-horizon downstream tasks such as VLN and ObjectNav. Humans explore by anchoring on transit nodes (doors, stairs, intersections), and VLMs can recognize these from RGB. Unifying exploration and memory building online should improve both coverage and memory quality.
key_idea: Fine-tune a VLM to predict Semantic Navigational Affordance (SNA) nodes and their connectivity from multiview RGB, and use these nodes as exploration subgoals while building a hierarchical scene-graph memory (SG-Memo) online.
insight: Using semantic transit nodes instead of geometric frontiers raises node recall and efficiency, and exploration that targets nodes yields a better memory than post-hoc construction. In Table 4(b), full ABot-Explorer reaches ObjectNav SR 65% versus 46% for the same trajectory processed offline and 33% for CogniPlan. Ablating edge prediction ('nodes only') drops performance in every scenario, e.g. MP3D CR_topo 58% versus 85%. Training on InteriorGS alone is comparable to HM3D-only, and joint training is best.
method: SNA VLM: Qwen2.5-VL-3B fine-tuned with SFT on 4-view RGB to output a local 2D graph: SNA nodes (room entry, stairs, intersection, normal) as pixel coordinates, traversability edges, room category and visible objects

Dataset: InteriorGS (1,000 scenes) manually annotated with SNA nodes and edges on occupancy maps; room labels via point-in-polygon; occlusion-culled visible objects via ray-casting; plus HM3D/MP3D scenes, about 500K VQA pairs
BEV lifting: pixel nodes are projected to the floor plane via inverse perspective mapping using camera intrinsics and extrinsics, giving a local 3D graph

Online SG-Memo update: new nodes are matched to the graph by a distance threshold; visited matches create edges, unvisited matches are merged by weighted averaging; pruning and connectivity-aware NMS yield the unvisited candidate set
VLM planner: the JSON-serialized SG-Memo goes to a VLM with a greedy prompt that prefers nodes aligned with the current heading and falls back to the farthest candidates for coverage
Memory consolidation: radius clustering keeps nodes by priority (stairs > room entries > intersections > normal), with majority vote for room type and set union for objects
Execution: ABot-N0 navigation policy handles local obstacle avoidance; stairs enable multi-floor transitions

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (SFT fine-tuned) for SNA perception; a VLM planner for subgoal selection; ABot-N0 as low-level nav policy
setting.training_data: InteriorGS (1,000 scenes, manual SNA annotations), plus HM3D (145 scenes; 136 multi-floor for training) and MP3D (34) in the full model; about 500K VQA pairs
setting.observation: four ground-parallel RGB cameras (90° yaw offsets, 720x640, 110°x104° FOV), RGB only
setting.action_space: high-level SNA node subgoals executed by a navigation policy (ABot-N0) via low-level continuous control
setting.privileged: none at test time (camera extrinsics calibrated; ground-truth used only for evaluation). Table 1 marks the method as 'use depth input ✓'.

numbers_note: Only custom exploration benchmarks are reported; no standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks. The paper's own ablation Table 5 (training data) lists CR_o/CR_t/AUC_o/AUC_t of 79/82/57/62 for the Full variant. Its numbers differ from the HM3D row of Table 1 for the InteriorGS-only variant (71/71/55/54). Table 1 labels the method as using depth while the text says RGB-only.
results: ABot-Explorer beats depth-based baselines (RRT, GLEAM, CogniPlan) on node coverage and efficiency in all scenarios. It reaches e.g. CR_topo of 96% on seen InteriorGS and 85% on MP3D versus CogniPlan's 69%. It trails CogniPlan on occupancy metrics in unseen InteriorGS (79 vs 81 CR_occ). Its online SG-Memo gives ObjectNav SR 65% versus 33% for CogniPlan-based memory, and multi-floor exploration reaches CR_occ 72% versus 35%.
limitations: Occupancy coverage on unseen InteriorGS is slightly below CogniPlan, a deliberate trade-off toward node coverage
Relies on manually annotated SNA data and IPM planar floor assumptions; VLM inference runs offboard on an RTX 4090; real-world evaluation is only qualitative
Evaluation is on custom benchmarks with few scenes (143) and inconsistent depth/RGB-only claims
